validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: solid. This is a real, FERC-certificated segment of the Florida Gas Transmission interstate system (Docket CP00-40), correctly classified as an operating natural-gas transmission expansion. Confirmed by: (1) FERC's own Federal Register notices for Docket CP00-40 (govinfo.gov FR-2001-07-19 / 01-18025, and federalregister.gov full-text 00-22258) describing the Phase V Expansion Project in Mississippi/Alabama/Florida; (2) two independent trade-press articles (Oil & Gas Journal 2003 'Florida Gas Transmission completes Phase V expansion, begins Phase VI'; IndustrialInfo.com 2001) describing the same project's construction and completion; (3) EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects: Historical Projects' table (the same source GEM's wiki page footnotes as [4]), which carries a discrete line item 'FGT Phase V Stage 4' -- Completed 2003-05-01, States MS/AL/FL, Cost $132M, Miles 136, Additional Capacity 130 MMcf/d, Diameter 24/36/16 in, Docket CP00-40 -- an EXACT match to every value on this GEM row; (4) Energy Transfer's own current (June 2026) 'FGT Phase IX' factsheet PDF, confirming FGT is still an active, operating interstate system today ('FGT is a subsidiary of Citrus LLC, a partnership between Energy Transfer and Kinder Morgan. The pipeline is operated by Energy Transfer'). No hallucination/GEM-only-entity risk here.

DUPLICATE check against the roster: P4035 (Stage 4, 136mi, MS-AL-FL, completed 2003-05) is NOT the same physical facility as sibling rows P4036 ('Phase V Stage 3', 15mi, FL only, completed 2002-12) or P4037 ('Phase V Stages 1-2', 64mi, MS-AL-FL, completed 2002-04) -- EIA's Historical Projects table treats all three as separate FERC-tracked project/completion milestones under the same certificate (CP00-40), consistent with how GEM already splits other multi-phase FGT expansions (Phase VI/VII/VIII each get their own row too). Recommend no merge.

SPEC CAVEAT (why this isn't a plain pass): summed across the three Phase V stage rows, GEM/EIA give 136+15+64 = 215 miles and 130+180+298 = 608 MMcf/d of stage-level 'additional capacity'. Two independent sources describing Phase V as a WHOLE project instead report ~165.8-167 miles of new pipe (FR-2001-07-19 final EIS-availability notice: 'approximately 165.8 miles of pipeline and 125,215 HP'; OGJ 2003: '167 miles of new pipeline and 132,615 hp'; IndustrialInfo 2001: '167 miles ... $452 million') and a net 428 MMcf/d capacity increase (OGJ, IndustrialInfo, both). That is a ~30% mileage overage and a ~42% capacity overage versus the aggregate figures -- a real inconsistency, not proof Stage 4's own 136mi/130MMcfd is wrong. Two innocent explanations exist and I could not rule between them: (a) capacity additions on sequential looped segments of one system are not simply additive end-to-end (the smallest downstream link caps net throughput), which plausibly explains the capacity gap alone; (b) FGT's original Dec-1, 1999 application (federalregister.gov full-text 00-22258, footnote 1) was for 'about 215.4 miles of pipeline, 15.7 miles of rehabilitated mainline' -- almost exactly the stage-level sum -- then was amended down to 191.5mi (Aug 2000) and again to ~165.8mi by the final July 2001 certificate; EIA's per-stage entries may trace to an earlier proposal iteration rather than final as-built facilities. Cross-checked against 8 OTHER FGT sub-project rows in this same EIA table (Phase IV, VI, VII Phase 1, VIII, Turkey Point Lateral, East Leg, Alabama Power Lateral, Mobile Bay Lateral -- see cross_row_leads) and every one of those EIA figures is an EXACT match to GEM's existing sheet values, so EIA is not a generally unreliable source here -- the Phase V 3-way split is the one place in this family where the parts don't cleanly reconcile to the reported whole. Recommend pulling FERC's actual certificate order (96 FERC P61,143, issued 7/27/2001, Docket CP00-40) for its per-facility mileage table before treating either the stage split or the aggregate figures as the final word; I could not reach the order text itself (elibrary.ferc.gov requires an interactive docket search, not a static URL).
